---
title: "Manifold"
subtitle: "Run Hello Pico on Manifold — the runtime host for a single Pico."
---

Welcome to **Manifold**, the first runtime-focused course of the Open
Engineering Academy. This course frames the smallest honest runtime
story for a single Pico: one Pico Element, hosted by **Manifold** on a
local Kubernetes cluster, wired through one **Wrangler**-declared
Channel, receiving one event and producing one observable response.

## Where this course fits

Manifold is a **runtime course**, not a fourth phase alongside compose /
construct / behave. The three-layer story still holds:

> **Crossplane composes**, **Sandcastle constructs**, **Picos behave**.

Manifold names the runtime host on which behaviour is observed. Under
the [Phase 7 constructive-realization contract](../../templates/README.qmd),
the role assignments this course teaches are:

| Tool           | Runtime role                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Kubernetes     | `RuntimeSubstrate` — the underlying execution layer                       |
| Manifold       | `RuntimeEnvironment` — Kubernetes-hosted host for Pico Elements           |
| Pico engine    | The in-process host inside Manifold that runs Pico Elements               |
| Wrangler       | `InteractionTopology` authoring — declares Channels and subscriptions     |
| Crossplane     | Realization step — composes runtime resources onto the substrate          |
| Sandcastle     | Realization step — constructs the executable form of a Pico               |

::: {.callout-important title="Scope — one Pico, one event, one response"}
This course keeps the runtime story narrow on purpose. It covers **one
Pico**, hosted by **one Manifold RuntimeEnvironment**, wired through
**one Wrangler Channel**, receiving **one event** and producing **one
observable response**. Multi-Pico topologies, fleet orchestration,
graphical control surfaces (for example, Home Assistant), and
non-Kubernetes runtimes are explicitly out of scope for this first
runtime course.
:::

## What you will learn

By the end of the course you will be able to:

- Describe what a **RuntimeSubstrate**, a **RuntimeEnvironment**, an
  **InteractionTopology**, a **Channel**, an **EventType**, and an
  **Observation** are, using the Phase 7 vocabulary.
- Explain how a Pico Element produced by the
  [Hello Pico lab](../../labs/hello-pico/index.qmd) is *hosted* by a
  Manifold RuntimeEnvironment without being *replaced* by it.
- Explain how a Wrangler-declared Channel wires exactly one event into
  the hosted Pico and how the resulting response is observed.
- Run the accompanying
  [Hello Pico on Manifold lab](../../labs/hello-pico-on-manifold/index.qmd)
  end-to-end on a local minikube cluster and capture the single
  observed response as the lab's produced artifact.

See the course descriptor in [`metadata.yaml`](metadata.yaml) for the
machine-readable summary (id, level, duration, prerequisites,
`runtime_substrate`, `runs_on`).

## Prerequisites

- Completion of the [Pico course](../pico/index.html), or equivalent
  familiarity with Rules, the Parser, the Composer, and the
  `hello-world-pico` artifact.
- Completion of the
  [Kubernetes setup foundation](../kubernetes/index.html) so `docker`,
  `minikube`, and `kubectl` resolve on your `PATH`.
- Familiarity with the [Crossplane course](../crossplane/index.html)
  and the
  [Hello Pico on Kubernetes lab](../../labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/index.qmd)
  is helpful but not required; this course consumes their outputs
  rather than replaces them.

## How this course is structured

This first runtime course is intentionally small: an overview page
(this file), a shared glossary, and one runnable lab. It does not yet
carry a Part 1 / Part 2 / Part 3 structure — the runtime story is
scoped to a single Pico so that later curriculum waves can extend it
without retrofitting.

```
courses/manifold/
  _quarto.yml          # this course website
  index.qmd            # you are here
  metadata.yaml        # machine-readable course descriptor
  glossary.qmd         # course glossary
```

The runnable material lives in the reusable lab:

- [Hello Pico on Manifold lab](../../labs/hello-pico-on-manifold/index.qmd)
  — deploy a Manifold RuntimeEnvironment onto a local minikube cluster,
  host a single Pico inside it via a Wrangler-declared Channel, send
  one event, and observe one response.

## What you will produce

A single artifact directory named `hello-world-pico-on-manifold` — the
lab captures the exact manifests applied to the cluster, the Wrangler
channel spec, the one event sent in, and the one observed response
line printed by the hosted Pico. This matches the `produces` entry in
[`metadata.yaml`](metadata.yaml).

## Start here

- [Hello Pico on Manifold lab](../../labs/hello-pico-on-manifold/index.qmd)
  — the single runnable path for this course.
- [Hello Two Picos lab](../../labs/hello-two-picos/index.qmd) — the
  first multi-Pico runtime lab that builds directly on Hello Pico on
  Manifold. It reuses the same Manifold RuntimeEnvironment on
  Kubernetes and adds a second named Pico plus one
  Wrangler-declared producer→consumer wiring. Run it after Hello
  Pico on Manifold when you are ready for the smallest honest
  two-Pico interaction.
- [Glossary](glossary.qmd) — course-scoped vocabulary aligned with the
  Phase 7 constructive-realization contract.

::: {.callout-note title="Course status"}
This is the first runtime-focused milestone of the academy. It
deliberately covers one Pico, one Channel, one event, and one
observation. Broader topologies, additional Control Surfaces, and
non-Kubernetes runtime substrates are deferred to later curriculum
waves.
:::
